prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2025-10-30. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 1.55 |
| Retained earnings       | 22,252M |
| Current liabilities     | 40,141M |
| Current assets          | 62,071M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 23,793M |
| Total liabilities       | 91,085M |
| Total assets            | 114,935M |
| EBIT / operating income | 8,386M |
| Revenue                 | 17,601M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2025-10-30, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The provided data imply a highly leveraged balance sheet (equity = 21 % of assets; total liabilities/assets = 79 %) together with an Altman Z-score of approximately 1.05, which lies in the distress zone. Liquidity is only adequate (current ratio 1.55) and the absence of any interest-coverage data precludes an investment-grade conclusion. These metrics map most closely to the BB region on the 21-grade scale.
DECISION: BB
